"""Everything a reasoning checkpoint may look at, as plain text and numbers, built once from a finished run.
No engine object leaks through: a model sees this and nothing else."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Evidence:
    data_dir: Path
    files: frozenset[str]  # the names of the run's input files: the only files a tool may open
    last_year: int = 2024  # the last year of the reporting period; a later date in a data line is not plausible
    rules: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # clause name -> text
    calculations: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # calc id -> record as text
    lineage: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # row id -> its source lines as text
    related: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # group account -> mapped local accounts as text
    results: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)  # calc id -> its result
    normal_sides: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # row calc id -> "debit" or "credit"
    # flag or concern -> the file:line or calc ids the rules already confirm
    confirmed: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def lines(self, file: str) -> list[str]:
        return (self.data_dir / file).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    # file:line of an fx_rates row -> percent from the median of its pair's other rates (the D15 measure)
    rate_gaps: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    rate_tolerance: Decimal = Decimal(10)  # A14
    # file:line of a map row whose name reads as one nature and whose group account has that same nature
    nature_agrees: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
"""What a reasoning checkpoint may say. Every field is text or a menu choice: there is no number field and no field
that can name a disposition, so a model's output cannot become a figure or a decision."""
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

InputFlag = Literal[
    "no_valid_name", "value_not_plausible", "label_contradicts_meaning", "near_miss_of_expected",
    "inconsistent_with_neighbours", "nature_mismatch", "unit_or_direction_suspect",
]
CalcConcern = Literal[
    "sign_implausible", "magnitude_implausible", "formula_does_not_fit_nature", "inconsistent_with_related",
]


class LineClaim(BaseModel):
    cite: str = Field(description="the line, as file:line")
    flag: InputFlag
    reason: str = Field(max_length=300, description="one short sentence")
    quoted: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=6, description="exact pieces of the cited line")


class InputReading(BaseModel):
    claims: list[LineClaim] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=30)


class CalcClaim(BaseModel):
    cite: str = Field(description="the calculation id, for example fig:total_assets")
    concern: CalcConcern
    reason: str = Field(max_length=300, description="one short sentence")
    quoted: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=6, description="exact pieces of the record")


class CalcReview(BaseModel):
    claims: list[CalcClaim] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=12)


class TraceStepClaim(BaseModel):
    cite: str = Field(description="a source file:line or a calculation id")
    note: str = Field(max_length=200, description="what this step shows, in one short sentence")
    quoted: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=6)


class Investigation(BaseModel):
    """The chain from an output row back to the source lines. It reports; it never proposes a corrected value."""

    chain: list[TraceStepClaim] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=6)
    cause: str = Field(max_length=300, default="", description="which input looks wrong and what else it feeds")

means "the code could not tell", never "the code looked and disagreed".

**Seeded-fault evaluation** (`tests/evals/seeded_faults.py`). Plants six faults in a copy of the data (closing rate x100,
a journal amount typo, a map row moved from Revenue to Tax, a TB label that contradicts its map name, a journal year
typo, a duplicated intercompany invoice), finds the changed lines by diffing, runs the reasoning layer on the copy and
reports per fault hit or miss, plus false alarms (kept claims on lines no fault touched). A fault is hit when a kept
reader claim names one of its lines, or a kept calculation concern is built from one. It also lists which rule findings
point at each fault's lines (journal findings carry no line number, so that column understates the rules). No finding
or verdict is put in a packet; a test checks the packet keys and text. `python -m tests.evals.seeded_faults --live`
calls the configured model and writes `.northwind/seeded_faults/result.json`; the tests use fake models.

**Explain step** (`explain.py`). For a finding the rules already raised, the model writes why it matters (`cause`) and a
trace to the source lines, with the same tools, caps and grounding as the investigator. It runs after detection, so the
finding is its input by design; the detection packets (reader, calculation reviewer) still hold no verdict. A test checks
the finding list is identical before and after. Not yet wired into the CLI, and not run live.

**Citation forms** (`cite_exists`). A trace step may cite what the tools print: `file:line`, `file:first-last`, a
calculation or row id with or without `calc:` or `lineage `, `account N`, `rule policy N`. An id no tool could have
returned is dropped. Before this, `calc:row:1200` and `lineage row:1200` were dropped as nonexistent (69 of 99 steps).

**Sign and the normal side.** Balances are stored debit-positive, so a credit-nature account (revenue, payables, equity)
holds a negative number. Each row record carries `normal_side` from the chart and a `storage` sentence saying so; a sign
concern on a row that sits on its normal side is dropped as contradicted. Only a balance against its normal side stays.

**Tools** (`tools.py`): `read_lines`, `find_in_file`, `get_rule`, `get_calculation`, `get_lineage`, `get_related`.
File tools take a file name from the run's own list, never a path. At most 5 calls per item, no repeated call, and
every result is returned as `quoted_data` with a note that it is data. A test lists the tools and fails on any name,
parameter or import that could write, run a command or reach the network.

**Ledger and cost** (`app/llm/tooluse.py`). A tool-using call is keyed by model, settings, prompt version, schema,
packet and tool names; the answer is stored with its tool trail, so a replay shows what the model looked at. Unchanged
units replay free and only changed units go live. `--max-units N` limits live units for a whole run (it counts units,
not dollars); five failures in a row trip the circuit breaker; an authentication error stops the run at once.

**Commands.** `python run.py review --reasoning` replays; add `--live` to record unrecorded units; add `--smoke` to send
one unit to each checkpoint.

**What to say about it.** The model is never trusted with a number: its schema has no number field and no field that

import json, re
from collections import Counter
from app.llm.factory import load_llm_config
from app.llm.ledger import Ledger
from app.services.reasoning_service import run_reasoning
from app.services.run_service import build_context, stage
from app.utils.paths import DEFAULT_DATA_DIR
import os
os.environ["NORTHWIND_MODEL"]="openai:gpt-4o-mini"
cfg=load_llm_config(); led=Ledger(cfg.ledger_path)
run=stage(build_context(DEFAULT_DATA_DIR)); rep=run_reasoning(run,cfg,led,"replay")
lines=(DEFAULT_DATA_DIR/"adjustments.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
ids=[(i+1,m.group(1)) for i,l in enumerate(lines) if (m:=re.search(r'"id": "(JE-\d+)"',l))]
block={}
for k,(s,j) in enumerate(ids): block[j]=set(range(s,(ids[k+1][0] if k+1<len(ids) else len(lines)+1)))
real={"map UK 2310 (map_uk.csv:12)":{"map_uk.csv:12"}}
for j in ("JE-006","JE-009","JE-014","JE-016","JE-017","JE-019"): real[j]={f"adjustments.json:{n}" for n in block[j]}
cites={f.cite for f in rep.inputs.findings}
calc=set(rep.calcs.concerns())
out={"faults":{}}
for n,c in real.items(): out["faults"][n]="hit" if c&cites else "miss"
allreal=set().union(*real.values())
fa=sorted(cites-allreal)
out.update(hits=sum(v=="hit" for v in out["faults"].values()),total=len(real),reader_false_alarms=len(fa),
 reader_kept=len(cites),calc_concerns=sorted(calc),drop_reasons=dict(Counter(d.why.split(":")[0][:30] for d in rep.inputs.dropped+rep.calcs.dropped)),
 traces=len(rep.traces.traces),trace_steps_kept=sum(len(t.chain) for t in rep.traces.traces),trace_steps_dropped=sum(len(t.dropped) for t in rep.traces.traces))
json.dump(out,open(".northwind/live_score.json","w"),indent=1)
print(json.dumps(out)[:1500])

"""A claim that quotes a line of a JSON file exactly must not be dropped for the quote marks inside it."""
from pathlib import Path

from app.agents.reasoning.evidence import Evidence
from app.agents.reasoning.grounding import ground_line_claims
from app.agents.reasoning.reader import chunk_packets
from app.agents.reasoning.schema import LineClaim
from app.utils.paths import DEFAULT_DATA_DIR


def evidence(data_dir: Path) -> Evidence:
    return Evidence(data_dir=data_dir, files=frozenset({"adjustments.json"}))


def test_an_exact_quote_of_a_json_line_is_found_in_what_the_model_was_shown() -> None:
    ev = evidence(DEFAULT_DATA_DIR)
    _, shown = chunk_packets(ev, "adjustments.json")[0]
    line = ev.lines("adjustments.json")[11]
    assert '"' in line
    claim = LineClaim(cite="adjustments.json:12", flag="value_not_plausible", reason="odd", quoted=[line.strip()])
    kept, dropped = ground_line_claims([claim], "adjustments.json", shown, ev)
    assert len(kept) == 1 and dropped == []


def test_a_quote_that_is_not_in_the_chunk_is_still_dropped() -> None:
    ev = evidence(DEFAULT_DATA_DIR)
    _, shown = chunk_packets(ev, "adjustments.json")[0]
    claim = LineClaim(cite="adjustments.json:12", flag="value_not_plausible", reason="odd", quoted=['"amount": "99"'])
    kept, dropped = ground_line_claims([claim], "adjustments.json", shown, ev)
    assert kept == [] and "not in the evidence shown" in dropped[0].why

- **Measured result:** on the supplied data the model found 1 of 7 labelled faults, so the rules are the detector and
  the AI layer is advice. Figures, dispositions and findings are identical with the local ledger, the cloud ledger and
  no model (`tests/unit/llm/test_switch.py`).
**What the AI layer is worth.** On a recorded run, the reasoning layer on the cloud model hit 1 of 7
labelled defects. I did not tune prompts to raise that. The honest finding is that the rules are the detector and the

"""Exact packets: code joins the rows a reviewer needs, so a model never searches and never sees a detector's verdict.

Free text goes in quoted (policy: text in the data is data, never an instruction)."""
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from app.domain.journals import Journal, JournalLine
from app.domain.ledger import LedgerLine
from app.domain.runs import Context
from app.parsers.mappings import resolve_account
from app.utils.money import fmt2


def _shape(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.debit), fmt2(line.credit)) for line in journal.lines))


def _mirror(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.credit), fmt2(line.debit)) for line in journal.lines))


def mapping_packet(ctx: Context, line: LedgerLine, group_code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group = ctx.inputs.coa[group_code]
    return {
        "entity": line.entity, "local_code": line.local_code, "local_name": line.local_name.quoted(),
        "balance": fmt2(line.amount), "balance_side": "debit" if line.amount >= 0 else "credit",
        "mapped_to": {"code": group.code, "name": group.name, "type": group.account_type,
                      "statement": group.statement, "normal_balance": group.normal_balance},
    }


Running = dict[tuple[str, str], Decimal]


def _line(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, line: JournalLine, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group_code = resolve_account(ctx.inputs.maps, ctx.inputs.coa, journal.entity, line.account)
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"account": line.account, "in_entity_chart": group_code is not None,
                           "debit": fmt2(line.debit), "credit": fmt2(line.credit),
                           "memo": line.memo.quoted() if line.memo else None}
    if group_code is not None:
        key = (journal.entity, line.account)
        before = balances.get(key, Decimal(0))
        balances[key] = before + line.debit - line.credit
        out |= {"normal_balance": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].normal_balance,
                "statement": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].statement,
                "balance_before": fmt2(before), "balance_after": fmt2(balances[key])}
    return out


def journal_packet(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Balances run in file order, as D07 reads them: each journal sees the account as earlier journals left it."""
    others = [j for j in ctx.inputs.journals if j.id != journal.id and j.entity == journal.entity]
    return {
        "id": journal.id, "entity": journal.entity, "date": journal.date.isoformat(),
        "period": [ctx.policy.period.start.isoformat(), ctx.policy.period.end.isoformat()],
        "prepared_by": journal.prepared_by, "description": journal.description.quoted(),
        "lines": [_line(ctx, journal, line, balances) for line in journal.lines],
        "total_debit": fmt2(journal.total_debit()), "total_credit": fmt2(journal.total_credit()),
        "same_lines_as": [j.id for j in others if _shape(j) == _shape(journal)],
        "mirror_image_of": [j.id for j in others if _mirror(j) == _shape(journal)],
    }

1	"""The model comes from config/llm.toml, or from NORTHWIND_MODEL: a string like ollama:<name> or openai:<name>."""
2	import importlib
3	import os
4	import re
5	import tomllib
6	from pathlib import Path
7	from typing import Any
8	
9	from pydantic import BaseModel
10	from pydantic_ai.models import Model, infer_model
11	
12	from app.llm.ledger import LlmStop
13	from app.utils.env import load_env
14	from app.utils.paths import CONFIG_DIR, ROOT
15	
16	
17	class LlmConfig(BaseModel):
18	    model: str
19	    ledger: str
20	    max_output_tokens: int
21	    ollama_base_url: str
22	    request_timeout_s: float = 60
23	    settings: dict[str, float | int | str] = {}
24	
25	    @property
26	    def ledger_path(self) -> Path:
27	        return ROOT / self.ledger
28	
29	
30	def ledger_name(model: str) -> str:
31	    """One ledger file per model, named from the model string, so a cloud run never writes into the local file."""
32	    return "ledger/" + re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9.]+", "-", model.lower()).strip("-") + ".jsonl"
33	
34	
35	def load_llm_config(path: Path = CONFIG_DIR / "llm.toml") -> LlmConfig:
36	    """NORTHWIND_MODEL switches the model and nothing else: the ledger is derived from its name and the sampling
37	    settings come from the `cloud_settings` table (empty: determinism comes from the ledger, not from a seed)."""
38	    load_env()
39	    section = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["llm"]
40	    fields = {k: v for k, v in section.items() if k not in ("settings", "cloud_settings")}
41	    override = os.environ.get("NORTHWIND_MODEL", "").strip()
42	    if override and override != section["model"]:
43	        return LlmConfig(**{**fields, "model": override, "ledger": ledger_name(override)},
44	                         settings=section.get("cloud_settings", {}))
45	    return LlmConfig(**fields, settings=section.get("settings", {}))
46	
47	
48	def model_settings(cfg: LlmConfig) -> dict[str, Any]:
49	    """Only what config lists is sent (a cloud model may reject temperature or seed), plus the output cap. The
50	    pydantic-ai OpenAI model sends max_tokens as max_completion_tokens, the name the current API expects."""
51	    return {"max_tokens": cfg.max_output_tokens, **cfg.settings}
52	
53	
54	def build_model(cfg: LlmConfig) -> Model:
55	    provider, _, name = cfg.model.partition(":")
56	    if provider in ("ollama", "openai"):
57	        key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "")
58	        if provider == "openai" and not key:
59	            raise LlmStop("OPENAI_API_KEY is not set: paste it into .env (see .env.example) and run again")
60	        # loaded by name: openai is only in requirements-llm.txt, so a dev-only install must still type-check
61	        async_openai = importlib.import_module("openai").AsyncOpenAI
62	        from pydantic_ai.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel
63	        from pydantic_ai.providers.openai import OpenAIProvider
64	
65	        if provider == "ollama":
66	            client = async_openai(base_url=cfg.ollama_base_url, api_key="ollama", timeout=cfg.request_timeout_s)
67	        else:
68	            # retries are ours (client.py): the SDK would also retry a 429 that only means "out of credit"
69	            client = async_openai(api_key=key, timeout=cfg.request_timeout_s, max_retries=0)
70	        return OpenAIChatModel(name, provider=OpenAIProvider(openai_client=client))
71	    return infer_model(cfg.model)
72

1	"""Grounding: each claim in a verdict is checked on its own against the packet. A claim the packet does not support is
2	dropped and logged; the others stand. The same exact predicates feed the rule-based fallback."""
3	import json
4	import re
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	from decimal import Decimal
7	from typing import Any
8	
9	from app.agents.journal_reviewer.schema import JournalVerdict
10	from app.agents.mapping_reviewer.schema import MappingVerdictBase
11	from app.detectors.text_scan import PATTERNS
12	
13	MIN_SHARED = 2  # a name matches another account only if they share two words: one word ("costs") is not enough
14	
15	
16	@dataclass(frozen=True)
17	class Grounded:
18	    verified: tuple[str, ...]
19	    dropped: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
20	    unverified: tuple[str, ...] = ()
21	
22	    @property
23	    def risk(self) -> bool:
24	        """Only verified claims count."""
25	        return bool(self.verified)
26	
27	
28	def journal_facts(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, bool]:
29	    """What the packet proves, category by category. Wording of free text cannot be proved, so it is not here."""
30	    start, end = packet["period"]
31	    lines = packet["lines"]
32	    flips = False
33	    for line in lines:
34	        if line.get("statement") != "BS":
35	            continue
36	        before, after = Decimal(line["balance_before"]), Decimal(line["balance_after"])
37	        flips |= (after > 0 >= before) if line["normal_balance"] == "Credit" else (after < 0 <= before)
38	    return {
39	        "unbalanced": packet["total_debit"] != packet["total_credit"],
40	        "outside_period": not start <= packet["date"] <= end,
41	        "account_not_in_chart": any(not line["in_entity_chart"] for line in lines),
42	        "duplicate_of_another": bool(packet["same_lines_as"]),
43	        "reversal_of_another": bool(packet["mirror_image_of"]),
44	        "exceeds_balance": flips,
45	    }
46	
47	
48	def _texts(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
49	    quoted = [packet["description"], *(line["memo"] for line in packet["lines"] if line["memo"])]
50	    return [json.loads(q) for q in quoted]
51	
52	
53	def ground_journal(verdict: JournalVerdict, packet: dict[str, Any]) -> Grounded:
54	    facts = journal_facts(packet)
55	    verified: list[str] = []
56	    dropped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
57	    unverified: list[str] = []
58	    for flag in verdict.flags:
59	        if flag == "text_contains_instruction":
60	            lexicon = any(p.search(t) for t in _texts(packet) for p in PATTERNS)
61	            (verified if lexicon else unverified).append(flag)
62	        elif facts[flag]:
63	            verified.append(flag)
64	        else:
65	            dropped.append((flag, f"the supplied data does not support {flag}"))
66	    return Grounded(tuple(verified), tuple(dropped), tuple(unverified))
67	
68	
69	def _words(text: str) -> set[str]:
70	    return {w for w in re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower()) if len(w) > 3}
71	
72	
73	def mapping_facts(packet: dict[str, Any], coa: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> tuple[dict[str, bool], str]:
74	    """Exact sign test, and the best other group account by shared words with the local name (or "none")."""
75	    mapped = packet["mapped_to"]
76	    local = _words(json.loads(packet["local_name"]))
77	    own = len(local & _words(mapped["name"]))
78	    best, best_score = "none", max(own, MIN_SHARED - 1)
79	    for code, account in sorted(coa.items()):
80	        score = len(local & _words(account["name"]))
81	        if code != mapped["code"] and score > best_score:
82	            best, best_score = code, score
83	    side, normal = packet["balance_side"], mapped["normal_balance"]
84	    return {
85	        "sign_unusual": Decimal(packet["balance"]) != 0 and side != normal.lower(),
86	        "name_mismatch": best != "none",
87	        "wrong_statement_type": best != "none" and coa[best]["statement"] != mapped["statement"],
88	    }, best
89	
90	
91	def _mapping_claim_holds(flag: str, proposed: str, packet: dict[str, Any], coa: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> bool:
92	    mapped = packet["mapped_to"]
93	    if flag == "sign_unusual":
94	        return mapping_facts(packet, coa)[0][flag]
95	    if proposed == "none" or proposed not in coa or proposed == mapped["code"]:
96	        return False
97	    if flag == "wrong_statement_type":
98	        return coa[proposed]["statement"] != mapped["statement"]
99	    local = _words(json.loads(packet["local_name"]))
100	    shared = len(local & _words(coa[proposed]["name"]))
101	    return shared >= MIN_SHARED and shared > len(local & _words(mapped["name"]))
102	
103	
104	def ground_mapping(verdict: MappingVerdictBase, packet: dict[str, Any], coa: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> Grounded:
105	    proposed = getattr(verdict, "better_group_code", "none")
106	    verified: list[str] = []
107	    dropped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
108	    for flag in verdict.flags:
109	        if _mapping_claim_holds(flag, proposed, packet, coa):
110	            verified.append(flag)
111	        else:
112	            dropped.append((flag, f"the supplied data does not support {flag}"))
113	    return Grounded(tuple(verified), tuple(dropped))
114

13	def load_prices(path: Path = CONFIG_DIR / "pricing.toml") -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
14	    return tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("models", {})

17	def cost_fields(model: str, usage: dict[str, Any], prices: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
18	    """cost_usd as a string (null when the model has no price) and the reason when it is null."""
19	    price = (prices if prices is not None else load_prices()).get(model)
20	    if price is None:
21	        return {"cost_usd": None, "cost_note": f"no price for {model} in config/pricing.toml"}
22	    cost = (Decimal(usage["input_tokens"]) * Decimal(price["input_per_million"])
23	            + Decimal(usage["output_tokens"]) * Decimal(price["output_per_million"])) / MILLION
24	    return {"cost_usd": str(cost.quantize(Decimal("0.000001"))), "cost_note": f"price status {price['status']}"}

27	@dataclass
28	class AgentCost:
29	    calls: int = 0
30	    input_tokens: int = 0
31	    output_tokens: int = 0
32	    recorded_cost: Decimal = Decimal(0)
33	    new_cost: Decimal = Decimal(0)
34	    unpriced: int = 0
35	    new_calls: int = 0
36	
37	
38	@dataclass
39	class CostReport:
40	    per_agent: dict[str, AgentCost] = field(default_factory=dict)
41	
42	    def total(self) -> AgentCost:
43	        whole = AgentCost()
44	        for a in self.per_agent.values():
45	            whole.calls += a.calls
46	            whole.new_calls += a.new_calls
47	            whole.input_tokens += a.input_tokens
48	            whole.output_tokens += a.output_tokens
49	            whole.recorded_cost += a.recorded_cost
50	            whole.new_cost += a.new_cost
51	            whole.unpriced += a.unpriced
52	        return whole
53	
54	
55	def build_report(entries: list[dict[str, Any]], new_keys: set[str]) -> CostReport:
56	    """The entries a run used. recorded_cost is what they cost when recorded; new_cost is only what this run spent."""
57	    report = CostReport()
58	    for entry in entries:
59	        row = report.per_agent.setdefault(entry["agent"], AgentCost())
60	        usage = entry.get("usage") or {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
61	        row.calls += 1
62	        row.input_tokens += usage["input_tokens"]
63	        row.output_tokens += usage["output_tokens"]
64	        cost = entry["cost_usd"] if "cost_usd" in entry else cost_fields(entry["model"], usage)["cost_usd"]
65	        if cost is None:
66	            row.unpriced += entry.get("usage") is not None
67	            continue
68	        row.recorded_cost += Decimal(cost)
69	        if entry["key"] in new_keys:
70	            row.new_cost += Decimal(cost)
71	    for entry in entries:
72	        if entry["key"] in new_keys:
73	            report.per_agent[entry["agent"]].new_calls += 1
74	    return report
75	
76	
77	def format_report(report: CostReport, model: str) -> list[str]:
78	    lines = [f"cost for {model} (an estimate from config/pricing.toml)"]
79	    for name, a in [*sorted(report.per_agent.items()), ("all agents", report.total())]:
80	        unpriced = f", {a.unpriced} calls without a price (cost null)" if a.unpriced else ""
81	        lines.append(f"  {name}: {a.calls} calls ({a.new_calls} new), {a.input_tokens} input and {a.output_tokens} "
82	                     f"output tokens, recorded cost ${a.recorded_cost}, new cost this run ${a.new_cost}{unpriced}")
83	    return lines

"""Plain text checks on one data line, shared by grounding and the contradiction checks."""
import re

DATE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(\d{1,4})[./-](\d{1,2})[./-](\d{1,4})(?![\d.])")
WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]{2,}")


def invalid_date(line: str, last_year: int) -> bool:
    """A date-shaped token that cannot be a date in this period: month or day out of range, or a year after it."""
    for a, b, c in DATE.findall(line):
        year, month, day = (int(a), int(b), int(c)) if len(a) == 4 else (int(c), int(b), int(a))
        if not (1 <= month <= 12 and 1 <= day <= 31 and 1900 <= year <= last_year):
            return True
    return False

48	  a package, each agent folder has its four files. There are two agents, the journal and the mapping reviewer.
49	- `test_architecture.py`: the import rules above.
50	- `test_bundle.py`: the 15 supplied data files hash to the values in `config/bundle_manifest.sha256`. In a fresh clone
51	  this checks the committed bytes, because `.gitattributes` stops git from changing line endings in the data folder.
52	
53	## Choices worth explaining
54	
55	- **Pinned requirements.** Exact versions, so a fresh clone installs what was tested. Pins were checked against PyPI
56	  on 2026-11-17. `requirements.txt` names the packages the code uses; `requirements-constraints.txt` is the full
57	  `pip freeze` of the tested environment and is pulled in with `-c`, so transitive packages are fixed too. A clean
58	  venv installed from these files freezes to exactly that list. The packages for `requirements-llm.txt` are not in
59	  the constraints file, and `google-genai` is left unpinned until Gemini is first used.
60	- **TOML for config.** YAML reads `0031` as the number 25; TOML refuses it.
61	- **No line-ending conversion for the data.** The first commit stored 12 CSV files with changed line endings; the
62	  second commit ("store data files byte for byte") corrected it.
63	
64	## Wave 1 module notes
65	
66	### utils (task 1.0)
67	- `money.py`: `to_decimal` builds a Decimal from a string or int and refuses a float. `round2` rounds half up and is called only when a figure is written (policy 7, assumption A13). The module sets 50 digits of precision, so translation is exact enough to round once at the end.
68	- `hashing.py`: SHA-256 helpers and `dumps`, the one JSON writer used for outputs and hashes. It writes a Decimal as a bare number without passing through a float.
69	- `paths.py`: repository paths. The data folder is a command-line option; the path here is only its default.
70	
71	### domain (task 1.1)
72	All models are frozen Pydantic classes in `app/domain/`. The plan called this `types.py`; the structure document is the master, so it is a folder.
73	- `refs.py`: `SourceRef` (file, line, hash of the raw row) is the unit of traceability. `Money` is a Decimal that refuses a float and is written as a string in JSON.
74	- `quarantine.py`: `Quarantined` wraps free text. It prints only its length; scanners read `.text`, everything else shows `quoted()`.
75	- `ledger.py`, `journals.py`: trial-balance lines (debit-positive), mapping rows, the chart of accounts, monthly rows, journals and their dispositions (POST, REJECT, HOLD).
76	- `findings.py`: one problem with `file:line`, the amount affected and what the system did. Two findings with the same key merge.
77	- `entries.py`: a `Posting` is one piece of a balance with its origin (IMPORT, JOURNAL, REVALUE, TRANSLATION, ELIMINATION, ACQUISITION) and source rows. An `Entry` must balance.
78	- `figures.py`: `Determined`, `Provisional` and `Unknown` form a union. An unknown figure carries a reason and has no value field.
79	- `policy.py`, `runs.py`: policy values, the assumptions registry, the parsed inputs and the run manifest.
80	
81	### evidence store (task 1.2)
82	`app/db/connection.py` opens SQLite and applies `schema.sql`; every JSON column has a `json_valid` check, so a malformed document cannot be stored. The service files each own one table family: runs, findings (upsert by key), facts (a decision is stale when its evidence hash changes), recorded AI calls, and origin rows with traces. The database is disposable and rebuilt on every run.
83	
84	### parsers (task 1.3)
85	Each input file has a contract in `app/parsers/contracts.py` (columns, decimal and date columns, allowed values). A file that breaks it raises `ContractError` with the file, line and reason. Only outer whitespace is trimmed, so `0031` stays text. `tb_adapters.py` reads the three layouts (debit/credit columns, one signed balance, amount plus Dr/Cr) into one `LedgerLine`, chosen from the header; an unknown header blocks that entity. `fx_rates.py` parses the direction of each rate from the convention column and answers in GBP terms: the product rule for GBP/INR is in `FxTable.units_per_gbp`, and a rate the file does not give returns None. `journals.py` keeps the line each journal and memo starts on, so a finding can point at `adjustments.json:112`.
86	
87	### detectors (task 1.4)
88	Each detector is a function from a `Context` (inputs, policy, assumptions) to findings. `registry.run_all` runs all fifteen and merges findings with the same key. D01 and D03 check balance; D02 checks mappings (including the exact-name rule that catches UK 2310 Deferred income mapped to Revenue); D04 to D07 check journals (period, duplicates, accounts through the entity map, reversals past zero); D08 needs rates; D09 to D11 tie files together; D12 scans free text; D13 notes the tax step and identical months; D14 flags exact duplicate rows; D15 flags a rate far from its neighbours or from the rate a booked amount implies (amber, tolerances A14 and A15 in `assumptions.toml`). Findings never change a number: the consolidation reads them only to decide a journal disposition (task 1.6).
89	
90	### mapping (task 1.5)
91	`classify_all` gives every trial-balance line a verdict and `apply_mapping` applies the assumption switches. A suspect mapping is only changed when a human decision in `config/overrides.toml` approves it (UK 2310 to 2300, status `open` until someone signs it off; `load_overrides` turns it into the `map_uk_2310` switch). Reversing it, by deleting the row, adds 180,000 GBP to group revenue and profit. Unmapped and ambiguous lines get no group account and are carried in a suspense line, so mapping never changes a total.
92	
93	### journals (task 1.6)
94	`core/post_journals.py` turns trial-balance lines into IMPORT postings and decides each journal: REJECT when invalid for FY2024 (unbalanced, outside the period, duplicate), HOLD when a human must look (account not in the entity chart, reversal past zero), otherwise POST. 95	
96	### revaluation and intercompany (task 1.7)
97	`core/revalue.py` restates a foreign-currency monetary line at the closing rate (policy 3) and books the difference to 7300; a line whose rate is missing is reported, never guessed. `core/intercompany.py` pairs the two sides by document reference, records an invoice the receiver has not booked at the closing rate (policy 5) and splits the difference into in-transit plus revaluation. 98	
99	### translate (task 1.8)
100	`core/translate.py` applies policy 2: closing rate for assets and liabilities, the average rate for the period the entity was owned for income and expenses. Which average applies is derived from the entity acquisition date and the rate windows in `fx_rates.csv`. Equity accounts are not translated here (group equity comes from `prior_year_group.csv` plus the reserve, see task 1.10). Every translated posting keeps its source rows and names the rate rows it used.
101	
102	### acquisition and elimination (task 1.9)
103	`core/acquisition.py` splits India nine-month trial balance at the completion month: income and expense come from the monthly file for the months owned, and profit before completion is carried to reserves. It also computes goodwill (consideration less 80% of net assets at completion, held in INR and retranslated at closing) and non-controlling interest (20% of net assets, proportionate method). `core/eliminate.py` builds the balanced elimination entries: intercompany balances, intercompany income and expense (the rate difference goes to 7300) and the two investments. 104	
105	### reserve, statements and figures (task 1.10)
106	`core/reserve.py` computes the translation reserve two ways. The balance route treats equity as fixed by net assets: the reserve is what remains after share capital, retained earnings (opening plus the owners share of profit) and non-controlling interest. The components route adds up named exchange differences: US opening net assets and profit, India net assets, profit and goodwill, less the retranslation of the two investments the group eliminates. The two must agree within a cent. `core/statements.py` builds the balance sheet, profit and loss and changes in equity. `core/figures.py` produces the twelve control figures; a figure that depends on the missing SGD rate is Provisional with that open item, and the SGD balance itself is Unknown with its reason.
107	
108	### policy binding (task 1.11)
109	`config/policy.toml` holds the policy values the engine reads (difference accounts, the intercompany residual account, the reporting period). It records the SHA-256 of `group_policies.md`. `check_binding` compares that hash with the file on every run; if the policy text changed and nobody re-approved `policy.toml`, the run is blocked and every figure is `null` with the reason. Reading clauses automatically is a Wave 3 task.
110	
111	### verification (task 1.12)
112	`app/verification/invariants.py` holds checks that must hold for any input; a failing check marks the run failed instead of being adjusted away. `app/verification/oracle.py` is a second implementation of the same method: it recomputes the control figures from the raw files with separate code (no imports from `core` or `parsers`), working per entity in local currency. 113	
114	### lineage, outputs and commands (task 1.13)
115	The investment-elimination balance check in `eliminate.investments` can never fail: account 3300 is a plug in both entries, so each entry balances by construction. 116	
117	### input validation (the bouncer)
118	Impossible inputs stop the run before any figure with a `ContractError` naming file, line and column. `finite_decimal` in `contracts.py` refuses text, NaN and infinity. `fx_rates.py` refuses a rate that is empty, zero or negative, and a second row for the same pair, rate type and date (in either direction), whether it repeats the first or conflicts with it. `tb_adapters.py` and `journals.py` refuse a line with both debit and credit filled, and a journal amount that is not a decimal. `check_percentage` accepts above 0 and up to 100 (the UK is 100) for `ownership_pct` and for the interest in the acquisition note. `ranges.py` checks, against the policy period, India's months, invoice dates, and that the closing and opening rates are dated at the year ends; journal dates are not checked there because a journal outside the year is a finding (JE-017). 119	
120	### run log (task 1.14)
121	`app/utils/logging.py` writes one JSON line per event to `.northwind/logs/`. 122	
123	## Wave 2 module notes
124	
125	### overrides and the review queue (task 2.2)

127	
128	### the LangGraph workflow (task 2.1)
129	`app/orchestrator/` runs five stages: intake, analyse, resolve, consolidate, export (`nodes.py`). `graph.py` wires them; after analyse, `edges.after_analyse` sends the run to resolve only if an override is open or stale. 130	
131	### the plain runner (task 2.3)
132	`runner_plain.run_plain` calls the same node functions in order, with no LangGraph. `python run.py consolidate --engine plain` uses it. 133	
134	### whatif, impact and diff-inputs (task 2.4)
135	`services/whatif_service.py` copies the input folder to a temporary directory, applies the change and runs the whole consolidation on the copy; the supplied files are never written (a test hashes them before and after). `python run.py whatif --patch fx_rates.csv:6.rate=1.30` sets one cell (line numbers count the header as 1, line endings are kept); `--append "fx_rates.csv=GBP,SGD,closing,1.7300,2024-12-31,SGD per 1 GBP"` adds a row; `--set je017=post` flips an assumption for that run. 136	
137	### perturbation and property tests (task 2.5)
138	`tests/perturbation/` changes one input at a time on a copy and checks two things: the invariants and the oracle still hold, and the figure moves by the amount worked out by hand (US revenue +1,000 USD gives +782.47 GBP at the 1.2780 average). 139	
140	### status sidecar and the strict control figures check (task 2.6)
141	`control_figures_pb.json` holds the 12 keys, each a number or `null` (`journals` is posted, rejected and held counts). 142	
143	## Wave 3 module notes
144	
145	### the model adapter and ledger (task 3.1)
146	`app/llm/` is the only place that imports `pydantic_ai`. `client.run_structured` makes one typed call. In `replay` mode (the default, and what a fresh clone uses) it answers from `ledger/<model>.jsonl` and raises `LedgerMiss` if the call was never recorded; it never makes a silent live call. In `live` mode it replays when the call is recorded, otherwise calls the model (at most two requests: one retry for malformed output) and appends the result, failures included. To say live: the local model is not repeatable even at temperature 0, so the ledger, not a seed, is what makes a run reproducible.

## Choices worth explaining

- **Pinned requirements.** Exact versions, so a fresh clone installs what was tested. Pins were checked against PyPI
  on 2026-11-17. `requirements.txt` names the packages the code uses; `requirements-constraints.txt` is the full
  `pip freeze` of the tested environment and is pulled in with `-c`, so transitive packages are fixed too. A clean
  venv installed from these files freezes to exactly that list. The packages for `requirements-llm.txt` are not in
  the constraints file, and `google-genai` is left unpinned until Gemini is first used.
- **TOML for config.** YAML reads `0031` as the number 25; TOML refuses it.
- **No line-ending conversion for the data.** The first commit stored 12 CSV files with changed line endings; the
  second commit ("store data files byte for byte") corrected it.

### status sidecar and the strict control figures check (task 2.6)
`control_figures_pb.json` holds the 12 keys, each a number or `null` (`journals` is posted, rejected and held counts). The reason for a `null` and the open items behind a provisional figure live in `control_figures_status.json`, so the required file keeps the shape the brief asks for. `tests/unit/writers/test_control_figures_schema.py` validates the file with a strict Pydantic model (no extra keys, no numbers as strings, no booleans) on the supplied data and on a blocked run, and checks that every `null` has a reason and every provisional figure names its open items.

## Wave 3 module notes

### the model adapter and ledger (task 3.1)
`app/llm/` is the only place that imports `pydantic_ai`. `client.run_structured` makes one typed call. In `replay` mode (the default, and what a fresh clone uses) it answers from `ledger/<model>.jsonl` and raises `LedgerMiss` if the call was never recorded; it never makes a silent live call. In `live` mode it replays when the call is recorded, otherwise calls the model (at most two requests: one retry for malformed output) and appends the result, failures included. The ledger key hashes the model, settings, prompt version, output schema and packet, so changing any of them forces a new recording. `factory.py` reads `config/llm.toml` and sends only the settings listed there (a cloud model may reject `temperature`). Callers catch `LlmUnavailable` and fall back to the rule-based proposer. The OpenAI client is imported inside `build_model`, so tests and CI need no `openai` package. To say live: the local model is not repeatable even at temperature 0, so the ledger, not a seed, is what makes a run reproducible.

148	### units, packets and the two reviewers (task 3.2)
149	`app/agents/review/units.py` lists what a reviewer is asked about: one unit per mapped trial-balance line (43) and one per journal (20). `packets.py` builds each packet by exact join: for a journal, the totals, the period, whether each account resolves in the entity's chart, the account balance before and after the line (in file order, as detector D07 reads it), and the ids of journals with the same lines or the mirror-image lines. Free text enters only as a quoted string. A packet never carries a detector verdict. `app/agents/review/verdict.py` is the shared base of every answer: one boolean per risk category and `risk` computed in code, so a model cannot say "no risk" while flagging a category. The journal reviewer has seven categories; the mapping reviewer three plus a `better_group_code` whose allowed values are generated from the chart of accounts. Only these two reviewers are built; invoices and FX lines are decided by rules (detectors D09 to D11), so a model adds nothing there. The prompt version of each reviewer is part of the ledger key.
150	
151	### grounding, fallback and the review service (task 3.3)
152	`app/agents/review/grounding.py` checks each claim in a verdict on its own against the packet. `journal_facts` proves unbalanced, outside period, account not in the chart, duplicate, mirror-image and exceeds-balance from numbers; a claim the packet does not support is dropped with a reason and the others stand. Wording claims (`text_contains_instruction`) cannot be proved from numbers: they are verified when the D12 lexicon matches and otherwise kept as `unverified`, which never counts as risk. A mapping claim needs a proposed account that exists in the chart; a name mismatch also needs the local name to share two words with that account's name and more than with the current one (one shared word, like "costs", gave six false alarms in a first try). `fallback.py` answers from the same exact facts when no recorded model answer exists, so a ledger miss degrades to rules, not to an error. `services/review_service.py` runs both reviewers over all 63 units: replay or record, ground, fall back. The result is advice and changes no figure (policy 2). On the supplied data the rule-based proposer flags exactly the six defective journals (JE-006, 009, 014, 016, 017, 019) and one mapping (UK 2310).
153	
154	### eval harness and injection tests (tasks 3.4 and 3.5)
155	`tests/evals/` measures agreement with deterministic checks on labels the author wrote; it is not an accuracy figure. The labels were written by the same AI tool that wrote the rule baseline, and the baseline shares its predicates (`journal_facts`, `mapping_facts`) with grounding, so the rules scoring well is partly by construction. It scores reviewer results with set arithmetic only, no judge model: recall of labelled defects, false alarm rate of verified claims, the share of claims grounding dropped, and exact matches per unit. Labels for the supplied data are in `labels.py` (six journals, one mapping, everything else clean); `seeds.py` adds seven journal and eight mapping units with one thing broken each, labelled by construction, to measure recall on cases the data does not contain. `python -m tests.evals.record --live` runs everything against the configured model, appends to the ledger, writes `.northwind/eval_results.json` and prints a few summary lines; without `--live` it replays. The rule-based proposer is the baseline: it finds every labelled journal defect from numbers, but cannot read the JE-006 memo's wording. `tests/redteam/` shows that the memo cannot change a disposition, a figure or a finding: removing it changes nothing, and a recorded answer from a model that obeyed it (all false) leaves the engine untouched while the review service marks the unit `missed=('unbalanced',)`, the model disagreeing with the rules.
156	
157	### the lexicon policy reader (task 3.6)
158	`app/parsers/policy_text.py` now also reads `group_policies.md` with a lexicon: for eight policy choices (translation of assets and liabilities, income and expenses and equity, monetary items, NCI measurement, goodwill translation, intercompany elimination, journal posting) it finds the sentence in the right clause and matches a few ways of saying each value ("closing", "year-end", "reporting date"). Each reading carries its clause number and the quoted sentence. A sentence it cannot read gives `None` with a reason, and one that matches two values is ambiguous: never a guess. `compare` sets the readings against `config/policy.toml`, and `run.py check` now reports any difference. The hash binding still decides whether a run may continue; the lexicon says why the approved config no longer matches a changed text. An LLM reader for clauses the lexicon cannot read is stretch work and not built.
159	
160	### the model switch and `run.py review` (task 3.7, local part)
161	Everything model-specific is in `config/llm.toml`: the model string (`ollama:`, `openai:`, `google:`, `anthropic:`), its settings (leave the table empty for a cloud model that rejects sampling parameters) and the ledger file. To switch: set `model` and `ledger`, put the provider's key in the environment (never in the repo), and run `python run.py review --live` once to record that model's answers; commit the new ledger file. The ledger key includes the model and settings, so the local ledger can never answer for a cloud model (a test proves a miss, then the rule fallback). `run.py review` prints the verified, unverified and missed claims per unit and how many units a model answered. Running it changes no figure: a test hashes the figures before and after. Not done here: a cloud recording, which needs an API key the repository does not hold.
162	
163	### running a cloud model safely (final development run)
164	**Add the key.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env`, paste the key after `OPENAI_API_KEY=` and set `NORTHWIND_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o-mini` (or export both in the shell). `app/utils/env.py` loads `.env` without overriding a variable that is already set. The key is read only from the environment. `scrub()` hides key-shaped text (`sk-...`, bearer tokens, the exact value of a key variable) before anything is written to the ledger or put in an error message, and the pre-commit check rejects staged text that looks like a key (a test value is marked `FAKE`). `.env` is gitignored.
165	
166	**Switch the model.** `NORTHWIND_MODEL` changes the model and nothing else: the ledger file is named from the model (`ledger/openai-gpt-4o-mini.jsonl`), so the local ledger is never touched, and the sampling settings come from the empty `[llm.cloud_settings]` table (determinism comes from the ledger; `seed` is documented as best effort). The output cap is sent as `max_completion_tokens`, the name the current API expects. Without a key a live run stops at once with a plain message.
167	
168	**Run it.** First `python -m tests.evals.record --live --smoke`: one journal and one mapping unit, then the tokens and cost. Then `python -m tests.evals.record --live` for the rest (units already recorded are replayed, never sent again). Both print about ten lines and never the raw answer. `python run.py review --live` records for the whole run, and `python run.py review --cost` prints the report.
169	
170	**Limits.** Each request times out after `request_timeout_s` (60). A call is at most two requests (one retry for a malformed answer). A 429 for rate and any 5xx are retried twice after a 2 s and an 8 s wait; a timeout is not retried. A 401, a 403 and a 429 that means no credit (`insufficient_quota`) raise `LlmStop`: the batch ends with the units left counted. After five live calls in a row fail or are unavailable the breaker stops the batch the same way. There is no dollar cap, so the number to watch is the call count in the summary.
171	
172	**Cost report.** `config/pricing.toml` holds the price per million tokens with its source URL and the date it was read; it stays ASSUMED until someone checks the page. Each recorded call stores its tokens and its cost (null with a reason for a model without a price). `review --cost` prints calls, tokens, recorded cost and new cost per agent: a replay shows 0 new cost and the cost recorded earlier. Costs go to the screen and the run log, never into the 12-figure outputs, which stay byte-identical (a test runs the figures with the local ledger, a fake cloud ledger and no model).
173	
174	**What the docs said, 2026-11-18.** `gpt-4o-mini` supports `json_schema` structured output; strict mode needs every property required and `additionalProperties: false`, which pydantic-ai's OpenAI schema transformer produces (checked on both reviewer schemas). The model page marks the dated snapshot `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` as deprecated while the alias is still listed: record early and expect to change the model string later.
175	
176	### results of the local model (task 3.4)
177	Recorded with `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` (78 units, ledger `ledger/qwen3-4b-dev.jsonl`, 83 lines; one seeded unit, `SEED-J-balanced`, timed out twice and is answered by the rule fallback). After grounding:
178	
179	| Reviewer | Units | Recall | False alarms | Claims dropped by grounding |
180	|---|---|---|---|---|
181	| Local model, supplied data | 63 | 0.33 | 0.00 | 0.62 |
182	| Local model, seeded | 14 | 0.17 | 0.00 | 0.71 |
183	| Rule-based baseline, supplied | 63 | 0.89 | 0.00 | 0 |
184	| Rule-based baseline, seeded | 15 | 0.46 | 0.00 | 0 |
185	
186	Read these as agreement with those checks, not accuracy. Part of the dropped share measures how strict the two-word name rule in grounding is. The model reliably found duplicates, the unbalanced journal and mirror images. It missed all three out-of-period dates, the exceeds-balance case and the unknown account, and its mapping claims mostly failed grounding (10 name-mismatch claims dropped, 9 real ones missed). Grounding removed every false claim (false alarms 0.00 after it), which is what it is for, but the cost is low recall: a 4B model is a weak second opinion here and the rules do better on every category they can compute. The rules cannot read wording, so the model's value is limited to cases like the reworded memo. Prompts were not tuned further (journal prompt on its second version, mapping on its first); the result is a finding, not a target. The sample is small and the labels are mine.
187	
188	### results of the cloud model (task 3.7)
189	Recorded with `openai:gpt-4o-mini` (78 units, 77 calls, ledger `ledger/openai-gpt-4o-mini.jsonl`; 34,525 input and 5,388 output tokens, about $0.008 at the ASSUMED prices in `config/pricing.toml`). Every unit was answered by the model, none by the fallback. Same wording rule as above: agreement with deterministic checks on author-written labels, not accuracy.
190	
191	| Reviewer | Units | Recall | False alarms | Claims dropped by grounding |
192	|---|---|---|---|---|
193	| Cloud model, supplied data | 63 | 0.56 | 0.00 | 0.80 |
194	| Cloud model, seeded | 15 | 0.29 | 0.00 | 0.60 |
195	| Local model, supplied data | 63 | 0.33 | 0.00 | 0.62 |
196	| Rule-based baseline, supplied | 63 | 0.89 | 0.00 | 0 |
197	| Rule-based baseline, seeded | 15 | 0.46 | 0.00 | 0 |
198	
199	On the six supplied journals the cloud model found five of the six defects (unbalanced, two duplicates, unknown account, out-of-period) and missed the exceeds-balance case. Its mapping answers were mostly dropped by grounding. It is a better second opinion than the 4B model, and still below the rules on everything the rules can compute. Prompts were not tuned after the first recording.
200	
201	For JE-006 the model said the entry is unbalanced and did not follow the memo; it did not flag the memo as an instruction (`text_contains_instruction` false), which the D12 lexicon does. A test replays that real answer and asserts that dispositions, the 12 figures and the findings are unchanged; another test shows they are identical with the local ledger, the cloud ledger and no model.
202	
203	
204	## The review page (wave 4)
205	
206	### what it is
207	`python run.py serve` starts FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8000 and serves `frontend/` at `/ui`. It adds no accounting and no model logic: every route calls a service that already existed. Say this in the live session: the page is a window onto the CLI's own paths, and a test proves it shows the same 12 figures as `run.py consolidate`.
208	
209	### the pieces
210	- `app/services/registry_service.py`: one folder per run under `.northwind/runs/<id>/` (`data/`, `config/`, `output/`, `run.db`, `checkpoints.db`, `logs/`, `run.json`). The config files are copied per run, so approving an override in the page edits that run's copy, never `config/overrides.toml`. The id must match a strict pattern before it touches the disk.
211	- `app/services/upload_service.py`: the 15 expected names, a 1 MB limit, and one existing parser per file. A body is checked in a scratch file and stored only if it passes, so the error shown on a row is the error the run would hit. Uploaded text is data: it is parsed, never run, and shown with text nodes.
212	- `app/services/pipeline_service.py`: `analyse` is the same graph as `run.py consolidate` (it pauses at the review gate), `decide` is `resume_graph`, `review_view` collects findings, dispositions, the queue and the advice, `build` re-runs the engine's 20 checks.
213	- Advice is replayed from the ledger only. A unit with no recorded answer falls back to the rules and the page says "not recorded". A test makes `build_model` raise and the review route still answers.
214	- `app/services/results_service.py`: reads `control_figures_pb.json` and `control_figures_status.json` (a null shows its reason), builds the zip (only names in the run's own output folder, plus `run_manifest.json`), and compares two runs with `diff_inputs` and `impact`.
215	- `app/routes.py`, `app/routes_results.py`, `app/api_models.py`, `app/main.py`: thin endpoints, strict request models, handlers that turn `UnknownRun` into 404, `NotReady` into 409 and bad input into 422.
216	
217	### the input workbench (item 1: rows and explain)
218	- `app/services/rows_service.py`: a source file as labelled rows. A CSV record, a journal in `adjustments.json` (at the line of its `"id"`, the line the journal findings cite) or a non-blank line of a markdown file is one row. A finding belongs to the last row starting at or before its cited line.
219	- `app/services/inputs_service.py`: `rows_view` puts each finding on its row; `row_explain_service.explain_row` adds the rule in plain words, the policy clause, the evidence cells and the recorded AI view. The AI view is attached to a finding only for D02 to D07 and D12, because the reviewers read journals and trial-balance mappings only; a row of a mapping file or a journal also states what the AI looked at when no rule found anything.
220	- `app/services/rule_text.py`: one sentence and one policy reference per detector, and which reviewer actions the workbench offers on it.
221	- Endpoints: `GET /api/runs/{id}/inputs/{file}/rows` and `GET /api/runs/{id}/inputs/{file}/rows/{line}/explain`. No model is called.
222	
223	### scan progress (item 2)
224	- `app/orchestrator/nodes.py`: the analyse stage now logs one `file scanned` event per file (with its finding count) before the `findings` event. The log is not an output, so no output hash moves.
225	- `app/services/scan_service.py`: `GET /api/runs/{id}/scan` reads the newest log of the run: a file with an event is scanned, one without is waiting, one not uploaded is missing; the scan is finished when the `findings` event exists. The Scan page starts the analysis and polls this every 300 ms, so the bar shows what the log holds.
226	
227	### home and upload (item 3)
228	- Home (`#/`): "Continue a run" takes a run id and opens the run at its next step (an unknown id says so); "Create a new run" takes a name and an optional sample start. The runs list stays below it.
229	- Upload: each of the 15 files has its own chooser, so files go in one at a time. The mark comes from the server: Uploaded (stored and valid), Rejected (the contract's reason is shown and nothing is stored) or Not uploaded. Next stays disabled until all 15 are in.
230	
231	### the input workbench (item 4)
232	- `frontend/workbench.js` is the Review inputs step: files on the left with an open/total badge, rows in the middle (red blocking, amber flagged, grey noted; each row also says its review status in words), and a drawer for the selected row. The page replaces the old review step; the recorded AI review in full is still there, under the rows.
233	- `app/services/decisions_service.py`: the reviewer's decisions, an append-only `decisions.json` in the run folder (finding key, pass or override, reviewer, note, evidence hash, time). The evidence hash covers the finding and the row's exact values, so a decision made on a row that later changes reads as stale. Open and stale are worked out when read.
234	- `app/services/review_actions_service.py`: `POST /api/runs/{id}/inputs/{file}/decisions`. Pass acknowledges and moves no figure; passing a finding about a held journal (D06, D07) also closes that held item, which the engine already treats as reviewed and out of the figures. Override is refused unless the table in `rule_text.py` allows it, and the only override with an engine mechanism is the mapping one (D02, while it waits). D06 and D07 are allowed by the spec table but the engine has no mechanism, so they are acknowledge-only for now and the drawer says so.
235	- A file's badge counts open and stale findings out of all findings on it. Notes need no decision, so a file with only notes reads "Notes only", not "Reviewed".
236	- Say in the live session: every number on this page is the engine's; the page records who looked and what they decided, and a click can never silently change money.
237	
238	### generate output (item 5)
239	- `app/services/generate_service.py`: `POST /api/runs/{id}/generate` works as soon as the run is scanned. With every item answered it is the normal build. With items still waiting, it runs the same consolidate and export nodes without the human gate, so the files are what the engine produces with nothing applied that nobody signed off, and the output is a Draft. The run keeps its status (awaiting review); `generated_for` stores the input hash the Draft was made on, so results and files open for it, and close again if an input or the config changes.
240	- `GET /api/runs/{id}/unanswered`: the engine items still waiting and the findings nobody has passed or overridden (notes need no decision). A held journal and its D06 or D07 finding are one problem and are counted once. Passing a finding clears it from this list; it does not move any figure. The Draft banner on the later pages and the Generate page read this list.
241	- Test worth quoting: the Draft's twelve control figures equal the figures of a run whose held items were approved, because held journals stay out of the figures either way.
242	- Final or Draft is decided by sign-off (see "Review UI: the seven stages" below) and written into `signoff.json` in the zip.
243	
244	### the seven stages
245	The stages are the ones in "Review UI: the seven stages" at the end of this guide: upload, scan, review inputs, choose outputs, generate, review outputs, done. Results, what-if and compare are one page reached from Done. A what-if patches a copy of the run's data (`file:LINE.column=value`, file must be one of the 15) and builds a new run beside the old one.
246	
247	### limits to state honestly
248	One user, no login, no concurrency control: it is a local tool. What-if edits one cell; assumption overrides are not offered. `group_policies.md` is checked only for being readable; the policy binding is still enforced when the run starts. The gate detail text is shown tidied (Decimal reprs and long fractions shortened) in the page only.
249	
250	
251	### the redesign (still no new accounting or model logic)
252	- Look: `frontend/style.css` is hand-written, a system font stack, light and dark through `prefers-color-scheme`, visible focus, colours chosen for WCAG AA contrast. The header shows the run name, status and current step; a left rail shows each step as done, current, needs you (blocked) or not yet. The "runs locally" line is the footer note.
253	- Numbers: `frontend/format.js` shows GBP with separators and two decimals in right-aligned tabular numerals. The server sends money as text and the page never turns it into an exponent. A null reads "Not determinable" with its reason in a callout; a provisional figure has a badge with the open item as its tooltip and as a callout (touch screens cannot hover).
254	- Issue cards: `app/services/cards_service.py` writes each headline from the finding itself (amounts tidied, for example "JE-006 does not balance: debits 51,200, credits 50,000"). The memo sentence is added only when a D12 finding lies inside that journal's lines, and it says "asks reviewers to skip the check" only if the memo's own words do. The AI line is agrees, disagrees, raised no claim or not reviewed, taken from the recorded review of the same journal or account; a finding with no matching unit says not reviewed. Dropped claims come from grounding.
255	- AI review panel: `app/services/ai_service.py` replays the ledger (never a live call) and returns every unit with its evidence packet, the model's recorded answer, the grounding verdict, tokens and cost. Totals are sums of those rows. The panel is labelled "recorded review". Build shows the stages from the run's own log files (times are when they were logged) and then the gates; nothing is animated.
256	- Output viewer: `app/services/output_service.py` lists each output with rows, bytes and sha256, opens a file as tables (JSON money is read as text, 500 rows at most, 2 MB cap, download always works) and sorts the issues for a file. An issue is traced to a file only when its input `file:line` appears in that file's `source_rows` (statements: in the accounts they list; control figures: the figure named in the claim). Everything else is listed as Run-wide, never guessed onto a file. Routes: `/output-files`, `/output-files/{name}`, `/output-files/{name}/issues`, `/output-files/{name}/download`.
257	- States: every step shows "Loading", a retryable error, or an empty message. A step that needs a finished run explains why it is held back: paused (how many items wait, go to Review), blocked (the blocking reason) or not analysed.
258	- Not verified in a browser: the paused-run message (the sample run never pauses; the logic is simple but only read, not clicked) and keyboard-only use beyond visible focus.
259	- Waiting items: `waiting_cards` in `cards_service.py` makes one card for each open or stale override, with its reason and the effect of approve and of reject (the override's own `effect_if_reversed`). The review step draws them first, with the name field and Submit below. Held journals are decided by the rules, not by a person, so they show as cards without buttons.
260	- Gate: `require_done` refuses every step after review with 409 naming the undecided items, so results and build cannot show a figure while an item feeding it is open. The page refuses an empty or nameless submit and disables Next until nothing is waiting. There is no person's decision for a held journal in the engine (the rules hold it), so only open and stale overrides block.
261	- Money on the API: `results_service._json` reads every non-integer number in an output file as a two-decimal string, so no float crosses the boundary (counts stay integers). `format.js` hands those strings straight to Intl.NumberFormat, which formats a decimal string exactly.
262	- Safety: `create_app` adds TrustedHostMiddleware (127.0.0.1 and localhost only) and every error handler, including a catch-all 500, passes its text through `scrub`, which keeps a file name and drops the folders. Tests use base_url http://127.0.0.1.
263	- AI line on a card: a unit that was reviewed and not flagged reads 'Reviewed by the AI, not flagged'; 'Not reviewed' is only for a finding with no unit. A D12 memo finding is tied to the journal whose lines hold it (JE-006), and the AI's other claims about that journal (unbalanced) are not counted as agreement on the text, since free text cannot be proved from the packet.
264	- Output views: file tables use the same GBP formatting as the figures table; a list in a JSON file is one cell with a line per entry; provisional figures that share a reason share one callout; the figure headline pattern had lost its word boundary (a stray control character), which left 'Sgd_bank_gbp' unnamed, now fixed and tested; dropped-claim text says 'the supplied data' not 'packet'. Runs can be archived (hidden, not deleted) and restored from the runs list.
265	- Switching output files was slow because each switch re-ran the engine and the ledger replay for the issue cards (about 70 ms), then fetched the file list again, and asked for the file and its issues one after the other. file.content:
### units, packets and the two reviewers (task 3.2)
`app/agents/review/units.py` lists what a reviewer is asked about: one unit per mapped trial-balance line (43) and one per journal (20). `packets.py` builds each packet by exact join: for a journal, the totals, the period, whether each account resolves in the entity's chart, the account balance before and after the line (in file order, as detector D07 reads it), and the ids of journals with the same lines or the mirror-image lines. Free text enters only as a quoted string. A packet never carries a detector verdict. `app/agents/review/verdict.py` is the shared base of every answer: one boolean per risk category and `risk` computed in code, so a model cannot say "no risk" while flagging a category. The journal reviewer has seven categories; the mapping reviewer three plus a `better_group_code` whose allowed values are generated from the chart of accounts. Only these two reviewers are built; invoices and FX lines are decided by rules (detectors D09 to D11), so a model adds nothing there. The prompt version of each reviewer is part of the ledger key.

### grounding, fallback and the review service (task 3.3)
`app/agents/review/grounding.py` checks each claim in a verdict on its own against the packet. `journal_facts` proves unbalanced, outside period, account not in the chart, duplicate, mirror-image and exceeds-balance from numbers; a claim the packet does not support is dropped with a reason and the others stand. Wording claims (`text_contains_instruction`) cannot be proved from numbers: they are verified when the D12 lexicon matches and otherwise kept as `unverified`, which never counts as risk. A mapping claim needs a proposed account that exists in the chart; a name mismatch also needs the local name to share two words with that account's name and more than with the current one (one shared word, like "costs", gave six false alarms in a first try). `fallback.py` answers from the same exact facts when no recorded model answer exists, so a ledger miss degrades to rules, not to an error. `services/review_service.py` runs both reviewers over all 63 units: replay or record, ground, fall back. The result is advice and changes no figure (policy 2). On the supplied data the rule-based proposer flags exactly the six defective journals (JE-006, 009, 014, 016, 017, 019) and one mapping (UK 2310).

### eval harness and injection tests (tasks 3.4 and 3.5)
`tests/evals/` measures agreement with deterministic checks on labels the author wrote; it is not an accuracy figure. The labels were written by the same AI tool that wrote the rule baseline, and the baseline shares its predicates (`journal_facts`, `mapping_facts`) with grounding, so the rules scoring well is partly by construction. It scores reviewer results with set arithmetic only, no judge model: recall of labelled defects, false alarm rate of verified claims, the share of claims grounding dropped, and exact matches per unit. Labels for the supplied data are in `labels.py` (six journals, one mapping, everything else clean); `seeds.py` adds seven journal and eight mapping units with one thing broken each, labelled by construction, to measure recall on cases the data does not contain. `python -m tests.evals.record --live` runs everything against the configured model, appends to the ledger, writes `.northwind/eval_results.json` and prints a few summary lines; without `--live` it replays. The rule-based proposer is the baseline: it finds every labelled journal defect from numbers, but cannot read the JE-006 memo's wording. `tests/redteam/` shows that the memo cannot change a disposition, a figure or a finding: removing it changes nothing, and a recorded answer from a model that obeyed it (all false) leaves the engine untouched while the review service marks the unit `missed=('unbalanced',)`, the model disagreeing with the rules.

### the lexicon policy reader (task 3.6)
`app/parsers/policy_text.py` now also reads `group_policies.md` with a lexicon: for eight policy choices (translation of assets and liabilities, income and expenses and equity, monetary items, NCI measurement, goodwill translation, intercompany elimination, journal posting) it finds the sentence in the right clause and matches a few ways of saying each value ("closing", "year-end", "reporting date"). Each reading carries its clause number and the quoted sentence. A sentence it cannot read gives `None` with a reason, and one that matches two values is ambiguous: never a guess. `compare` sets the readings against `config/policy.toml`, and `run.py check` now reports any difference. The hash binding still decides whether a run may continue; the lexicon says why the approved config no longer matches a changed text. An LLM reader for clauses the lexicon cannot read is stretch work and not built.

### the model switch and `run.py review` (task 3.7, local part)
Everything model-specific is in `config/llm.toml`: the model string (`ollama:`, `openai:`, `google:`, `anthropic:`), its settings (leave the table empty for a cloud model that rejects sampling parameters) and the ledger file. To switch: set `model` and `ledger`, put the provider's key in the environment (never in the repo), and run `python run.py review --live` once to record that model's answers; commit the new ledger file. The ledger key includes the model and settings, so the local ledger can never answer for a cloud model (a test proves a miss, then the rule fallback). `run.py review` prints the verified, unverified and missed claims per unit and how many units a model answered. Running it changes no figure: a test hashes the figures before and after. Not done here: a cloud recording, which needs an API key the repository does not hold.

### running a cloud model safely (final development run)
**Add the key.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env`, paste the key after `OPENAI_API_KEY=` and set `NORTHWIND_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o-mini` (or export both in the shell). `app/utils/env.py` loads `.env` without overriding a variable that is already set. The key is read only from the environment. `scrub()` hides key-shaped text (`sk-...`, bearer tokens, the exact value of a key variable) before anything is written to the ledger or put in an error message, and the pre-commit check rejects staged text that looks like a key (a test value is marked `FAKE`). `.env` is gitignored.

**Switch the model.** `NORTHWIND_MODEL` changes the model and nothing else: the ledger file is named from the model (`ledger/openai-gpt-4o-mini.jsonl`), so the local ledger is never touched, and the sampling settings come from the empty `[llm.cloud_settings]` table (determinism comes from the ledger; `seed` is documented as best effort). The output cap is sent as `max_completion_tokens`, the name the current API expects. Without a key a live run stops at once with a plain message.

**Run it.** First `python -m tests.evals.record --live --smoke`: one journal and one mapping unit, then the tokens and cost. Then `python -m tests.evals.record --live` for the rest (units already recorded are replayed, never sent again). Both print about ten lines and never the raw answer. `python run.py review --live` records for the whole run, and `python run.py review --cost` prints the report.

**Limits.** Each request times out after `request_timeout_s` (60). A call is at most two requests (one retry for a malformed answer). A 429 for rate and any 5xx are retried twice after a 2 s and an 8 s wait; a timeout is not retried. A 401, a 403 and a 429 that means no credit (`insufficient_quota`) raise `LlmStop`: the batch ends with the units left counted. After five live calls in a row fail or are unavailable the breaker stops the batch the same way. There is no dollar cap, so the number to watch is the call count in the summary.

**Cost report.** `config/pricing.toml` holds the price per million tokens with its source URL and the date it was read; it stays ASSUMED until someone checks the page. Each recorded call stores its tokens and its cost (null with a reason for a model without a price). `review --cost` prints calls, tokens, recorded cost and new cost per agent: a replay shows 0 new cost and the cost recorded earlier. Costs go to the screen and the run log, never into the 12-figure outputs, which stay byte-identical (a test runs the figures with the local ledger, a fake cloud ledger and no model).

**What the docs said, 2026-11-18.** `gpt-4o-mini` supports `json_schema` structured output; strict mode needs every property required and `additionalProperties: false`, which pydantic-ai's OpenAI schema transformer produces (checked on both reviewer schemas). The model page marks the dated snapshot `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` as deprecated while the alias is still listed: record early and expect to change the model string later.

### results of the local model (task 3.4)
Recorded with `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` (78 units, ledger `ledger/qwen3-4b-dev.jsonl`, 83 lines; one seeded unit, `SEED-J-balanced`, timed out twice and is answered by the rule fallback). After grounding:

| Reviewer | Units | Recall | False alarms | Claims dropped by grounding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local model, supplied data | 63 | 0.33 | 0.00 | 0.62 |
| Local model, seeded | 14 | 0.17 | 0.00 | 0.71 |
| Rule-based baseline, supplied | 63 | 0.89 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Rule-based baseline, seeded | 15 | 0.46 | 0.00 | 0 |

Read these as agreement with those checks, not accuracy. Part of the dropped share measures how strict the two-word name rule in grounding is. The model reliably found duplicates, the unbalanced journal and mirror images. It missed all three out-of-period dates, the exceeds-balance case and the unknown account, and its mapping claims mostly failed grounding (10 name-mismatch claims dropped, 9 real ones missed). Grounding removed every false claim (false alarms 0.00 after it), which is what it is for, but the cost is low recall: a 4B model is a weak second opinion here and the rules do better on every category they can compute. The rules cannot read wording, so the model's value is limited to cases like the reworded memo. Prompts were not tuned further (journal prompt on its second version, mapping on its first); the result is a finding, not a target. The sample is small and the labels are mine.

### results of the cloud model (task 3.7)
Recorded with `openai:gpt-4o-mini` (78 units, 77 calls, ledger `ledger/openai-gpt-4o-mini.jsonl`; 34,525 input and 5,388 output tokens, about $0.008 at the ASSUMED prices in `config/pricing.toml`). Every unit was answered by the model, none by the fallback. Same wording rule as above: agreement with deterministic checks on author-written labels, not accuracy.

| Reviewer | Units | Recall | False alarms | Claims dropped by grounding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cloud model, supplied data | 63 | 0.56 | 0.00 | 0.80 |
| Cloud model, seeded | 15 | 0.29 | 0.00 | 0.60 |
| Local model, supplied data | 63 | 0.33 | 0.00 | 0.62 |
| Rule-based baseline, supplied | 63 | 0.89 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Rule-based baseline, seeded | 15 | 0.46 | 0.00 | 0 |

On the six supplied journals the cloud model found five of the six defects (unbalanced, two duplicates, unknown account, out-of-period) and missed the exceeds-balance case. Its mapping answers were mostly dropped by grounding. It is a better second opinion than the 4B model, and still below the rules on everything the rules can compute. Prompts were not tuned after the first recording.

For JE-006 the model said the entry is unbalanced and did not follow the memo; it did not flag the memo as an instruction (`text_contains_instruction` false), which the D12 lexicon does. A test replays that real answer and asserts that dispositions, the 12 figures and the findings are unchanged; another test shows they are identical with the local ledger, the cloud ledger and no model.


## The review page (wave 4)

### what it is
`python run.py serve` starts FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8000 and serves `frontend/` at `/ui`. It adds no accounting and no model logic: every route calls a service that already existed. Say this in the live session: the page is a window onto the CLI's own paths, and a test proves it shows the same 12 figures as `run.py consolidate`.

### the pieces
